title: NYC Pharma Day:
headline: A father takes his son's rare disease to the people who make the medicine. One room: a father, a scientist and a drug company.
story: Keith McArthur leads CureGRIN. His son Bryson is 20 and has GRIN1 disorder. He stands in front of the staff of GRIN Therapeutics and calls them his heroes. The film shows why: almost 10 years to a diagnosis, a community that grew from seven families to hundreds, and a trial that 79% of families can not join today. Quinn and Bruce answer. It is not a recap of the day.

Loops: L1 “Who is he thanking, and why?” opens 0:00 and closes at 0:05. L2 “Does a treatment reach kids like his son?” opens 0:00 and closes in the button. L3 “What about the other 79%?” opens at 0:52 and closes at 1:15. Stakes: 79% of the families in the CureGRIN census can not join the trial today. 30 people in this community have died.
do: Open on Keith saying “you are my heroes”, with the hook text. Nothing else on frame 1.
Name supers lower left, 3 seconds, never before 0:03.
Cut between sentences. Quotes stay as spoken.
Check every morning B-roll clip on scrub before you use it.
dont: No logo, name or fade at 0:00.
Never say or show that GRI disorders can be prevented, that a cure is near, or that anyone is at fault.
Do not show the Zoom name tiles on the lunch room TV. Crop or blur them.
No close shots of slides with data, except the ones named here.
Never use the words “find your hive”.
